protocol:
1. Set up a PCR reaction at the bench using a single-channel adjustable micropipette, sterile tips from a blue tip box, a 0.2 mL PCR tube, tube racks, and labeled microcentrifuge tubes kept on ice in a green ice bucket.

2. Assemble the reaction by transferring liquid aliquots from multiple chilled labeled tubes into the 0.2 mL PCR tube, changing pipette tips between additions; no reagent identities or transfer volumes are visible.

3. Cap the assembled 0.2 mL PCR tube and keep it cold during handling.

4. Briefly centrifuge the capped PCR tube in a benchtop mini-centrifuge with a blue/yellow rotor to collect the reaction mixture at the bottom of the tube.

5. Place the centrifuged PCR tube into a Bio-Rad T100 thermal cycler block and close the heated lid.

6. Select and run the saved Bio-Rad T100 thermal cycler program named “PHANTA” with reaction volume set to 20 µL; the displayed cycling profile includes 95°C, 57°C, 72°C, and a final 12°C hold, with a repeated cycling segment shown on the program screen.
